nodes.text: Every Sabbath day he [David] would sit and study all day. On that day when he was to die, the Angel of Death stood before him and could not [prevail over] him, because his mouth did not cease from study. He said: What shall I do to him? He had a garden behind his house. The Angel of Death came, went up, and shook the trees. He went out to see. As he was going up the stairs, a step broke beneath him. He fell silent and died.

Mishnah: A man may not go out with a nailed sandal, nor with a single [sandal] when he has no wound on his foot, nor with *tefillin* [phylacteries], nor with an amulet when it is not from an expert, nor with a coat of mail, nor with a helmet, nor with greaves; and if he went out, he is not liable to a sin-offering.

The Sages taught: Which is a proven amulet? Any that has healed, and a second time, and a third; whether an amulet of writing or an amulet of roots, whether for a sick person who is in danger or a sick person who is not in danger;
not [only if] he has had a fit, but [even] so that he will not have a fit.
And one may tie [it] and untie [it] even in the public domain, provided that one does not tie it
to a bracelet or a ring and go out with it into the public domain, because of appearances.
But surely it was taught: Which is a proven amulet? Any that has healed three people alike.
It is not difficult: this one is for proving the man, that one is for proving the amulet.

Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me: three amulets for three men, three times each: the man is proven and the amulet is proven. Three amulets for three men, once each: the man is proven, the amulet is not proven. One amulet for three men: the amulet is proven, the man is not proven.

Rav Pappa asked: Three amulets for one man, what [is the ruling]? The amulet is certainly not proven; is the man proven or not proven? Do we say: Look, he has healed him? Or perhaps it is this man's *mazal* [fortune] that is receptive to writing? Let it stand.
Gemara: What are “knots”? Adda Mari said that Rav Nahman bar Barukh said that Rav Ashi bar Avin said that Rav Yehuda said: knots of madder.
Abaye said: Mother told me: three [knots] hold [the illness] in check, five heal, seven are effective even against witchcraft.

Mishnah: One may go out with a locust's egg, with a fox's tooth, and with a nail from a crucified man, for healing; [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir. And the Sages forbid [it] even on a weekday, because of the ways of the Amorites.

Gemara: “One may go out with a locust's egg”: which they use for earache. “And with a fox's tooth”: which they use for sleep, [the tooth] of a live one for one who sleeps, of a dead one for one who does not sleep. “And with a nail from a crucified man”: which they use for swelling.
[This accords with] Abaye and Rava, who both said: Anything that is [done] for healing is not [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites.

A *tanna* [reciter of traditions] recited the chapter of the Amorites before Rabbi Hiyya bar Avin. He said to him: All of them are [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites except for these: One who has a bone in his throat brings [a bone] of the same kind, puts it on his crown, and says thus: “One, one, go down; swallow, swallow, go down; one, one.” This is not [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites.
And one who stirs in front of chicks: this is [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites.
A woman who dances and counts seventy-one chicks so that they will not die: this is [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites.
A woman who dances for the *kutah* [a fermented dip], one who calls for silence for lentils, and one who shouts for split beans: this is [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites.
A woman who urinates in front of her pot so that it will cook quickly: this is [forbidden] as the ways of the Amorites.
But one may put a splinter of mulberry wood and pieces of broken glass into a pot so that it will cook quickly; and the Sages forbid broken glass because of the danger.
The Sages taught: One may put a lump of salt into a lamp so that it will shine and burn; and one may put mud and clay under a lamp so that it will last and burn.

Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said: One who pulls taut a thread of stitching on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering; and one who learns a single thing from a Magian is liable to death; and one who knows how to calculate the seasons and the constellations and does not calculate, it is forbidden to converse with him.

*Magushta* [Magianism]: Rav and Shmuel: one said: sorcery; and one said: blasphemy. Conclude that it is Rav who said blasphemy, since Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said that Rav said: One who learns a single thing from a Magian is liable to death. For if it should enter your mind [that it is] sorcery, surely it is written: “You shall not learn to do” (Deuteronomy 18:9): but you may learn in order to understand and to instruct. Conclude [so].

What is [the concern of] witchcraft? As in that [case] where Rav Hisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna were travelling in a boat. A certain noblewoman said to them: Seat me with you. And they did not seat her. She [uttered] a word [and] bound the boat; they [uttered] a word [and] released it. She said to them: What can I do to you,
since you do not wipe yourselves with a potsherd, nor kill lice on your clothes, nor pull out a vegetable and eat it from the bunch that the gardener has tied?

“One who scratches on his flesh”: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Sages: But did not Ben Stada bring witchcraft out of Egypt in a scratching on his flesh? They said to him: He was a madman, and one does not bring proof from madmen. [Addition from Hesronot ha-Shas: Ben Stada? He is Ben Pandira! Rav Hisda said: The husband was Stada, the lover was Pandira. The husband was Pappos ben Yehuda! His mother was Stada. His mother was Miriam, a dresser of women's hair! As they say in Pumbedita: *satat da*, this one strayed from her husband.]

Rav Pappa said: We have a tradition: a lion does not attack two [people]. But look, we see that it does attack! That is as Rami bar Abba [said], for Rami bar Abba said: A wild beast has no power over a person until he appears to it like an animal, as it is said: “Man in his honour does not abide; he is likened to the beasts; they are alike” (Psalms 49:13). Rabbi Hanina said: It is forbidden to sleep alone in a house, and whoever sleeps alone in a house, Lilith seizes him.
